name: Egogram
oneLine: A quick, intuitive bar chart of how much time you spend in each of the five functional ego states - a snapshot of a pattern, not a fixed trait.
whatYouDid: You read Zara's trip-planning message and had to spot which functional bar was tallest - noticing that "obviously, don't argue, I already booked it" repeated across four sentences is what makes it diagnosable, not any single line.
confusion: People treat an egogram as a fixed personality score, done once and true forever; the tell is Dusay's own constancy hypothesis - raise one bar on purpose and, by his theory, another will quietly drop to compensate, which only makes sense if the shape is dynamic, not fixed.

fromBook.quote: The idea is to draw a vertical bar above each ego-state label. The height of the bar shows how much of the time you use that functional part.

expand.definition: Jack Dusay's egogram plots relative time spent in CP, NP, A, FC and AC as a bar chart; only the relative heights matter to the comparison, not the absolute scale of any one bar.
expand.otherFraming: Dusay's constancy hypothesis treats psychic energy as roughly fixed in total - deliberately raising one bar, by practicing new behaviours, tends to lower another on its own, rather than requiring you to suppress the one you want less of directly.
expand.tryThisToday: Draw your own five-bar egogram for "today so far", then draw a second one for how you'd like it to look - pick one bar to deliberately raise tomorrow.
